To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there is a significant delay from the first symptoms to diagnosis of head and neck cancer; 2) the delay is associated with patient-related factors such as age, gender, education, and marital status; 3) there is a lack of knowledge of the risk factors of head and neck cancers in the community; 4) the delay is also associated with the lack of knowledge of head and neck symptoms; 5) patients are not aware of the need for a specialist opinion;
patients who present with head and neck cancer at a late stage tend to be male, older, and have a history of alcohol abuse.

the most important factor associated with presentation delay in patients with head and neck cancer was the presence of pain, and that this association was stronger for patients with cancer in the oropharynx.

the study of the factors associated with delay in presentation in head and neck cancer patients in a developing country.
the development of a new type of computerized tomography scanner.

there is a lack of evidence in the literature to support the use of any specific treatment modality for the management of head and neck cancer.

, the factors which are associated with the delay in presentation for patients with head and neck cancer are: the patients themselves, their families, the healthcare professionals and the healthcare systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are a variety of reasons for patients with head and neck cancers to present late to the hospital.

the delay in presentation of patients affected with head and neck cancers is due to the patients’ lack of awareness of their symptoms and the lack of knowledge on the part of the patients’ general practitioner of the signs and symptoms of these cancers.
there is no one single cause for presentation delay, rather a complex interaction of factors.
